securityObjectives.statement: Never disclose rows, columns, artifacts, changes, or command capability outside the application backend-authorized grant and current online authorization generation.
Never expose a partial, mixed-cursor, corrupt, unauthenticated, or wrong-scope collection as application data.
Preserve canonical transaction order, durable ownership fencing, and convergent recovery under replay, crash, stale owners, and hostile inputs.
Keep secrets out of browsers, artifacts, URLs, caches, logs, metrics, error messages, and images while supporting explicit rotation and recovery.
Bound adversarial resource use before allocation or durable growth and reject excess demand without partial publication.
Make mutation authority, idempotency, business effects, and canonical echo transactional and prevent optimistic state from becoming false canonical truth.

capabilities: deploy and configure the self-hosted composition
control infrastructure credentials and backup media
excludedCapabilities: weaken release invariants without an authority change

capabilities: authenticate principals and evaluate business authorization
issue signed dataset grants and execute business commands
excludedCapabilities: delegate authorization decisions to the browser

capabilities: hold a short-lived grant and materialize authorized collections
modify all client code and state, replay requests, retain received bytes, and send arbitrary protocol input
inspect URLs, caches, worker messages, memory, errors, and timing
observe, delay, drop, replay, fragment, reorder, and inject traffic outside authenticated transport
hold valid credentials for a different principal or tenant
choose adversarial scope values, commands, mutations, and request timing
publish malicious or compromised dependencies, images, and build inputs
exploit unpinned resolution and parser vulnerabilities
excludedCapabilities: alter verified immutable inputs without changing their digest

components.reason: It is the canonical application state and transaction-order authority.
notTrustedFor: protecting data after a privileged host compromise

components.reason: The application owns authentication, business authorization, projections, and business command semantics.
Its durable monotonic value defines the server disclosure fence.
Release code enforces grants and canonical delivery but remains an exposed parser and routing surface.
trustedFor: verified release behavior under declared assumptions
current-owner fencing and bounded protocol handling

components.reason: Durable control state is trusted only after integrity, ownership, and recovery checks.
It stores immutable bytes but provider metadata and possession of an object URL are not authorization or integrity roots.
trustedFor: durable byte storage under configured provider guarantees

components.reason: Authenticated catalog metadata is the artifact publication and identity authority.
trustedFor: trusted decoded length, digest, schema, scope, cursor, and format bindings

components.reason: Application-selected code executes validated business commands within the transactional contract.
trustedFor: declared command semantics after server authorization

components.reason: The application maintains this PostgreSQL relation as sync-ready authorization data.
trustedFor: projected authorized row membership at its canonical cursor

components.reason: The user controls client code, storage, memory, extensions, DevTools, and received bytes.
notTrustedFor: authorization, artifact authenticity, completeness, erasure, or secret custody
reporting trustworthy protocol or performance evidence without an independent oracle

components.reason: Shared and browser caches may retain, replay, or mis-key responses and cannot decide scope.
trustedFor: transport optimization only after exact capability and cache checks
notTrustedFor: tenant isolation, freshness, revocation, or artifact integrity

components.reason: Configured DNS and authenticated transport carry traffic but are exposed operational dependencies.
trustedFor: confidentiality and peer authentication only when correctly configured and validated

components.reason: Pinned inputs, provenance, scans, and independent review establish candidate identity.
trustedFor: immutable candidate construction when all release gates pass
notTrustedFor: unreviewed mutable tags or network-fetched scripts

components.reason: Logs, metrics, traces, and backups are privileged residual-data systems operated outside request paths.
trustedFor: declared retention and recovery when access-controlled
notTrustedFor: receiving bearer grants, row payloads, or signing keys

boundaries.crossing: bootstrap, artifact capability, range, stream, resume, status, and command protocol messages
requiredControls: server-side grant verification and online generation check
bounded maintained parsers, authenticated transport, explicit versions, origin policy, and rate limits
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Reject before disclosure or mutation and never publish partial client state.

requiredControls: TLS with peer-name and trust validation
timeouts, size limits, anti-replay semantics, and authenticated message ordering where transport does not provide it
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Do not fall back to plaintext or accept an unauthenticated endpoint.

boundaries.crossing: cacheable artifacts, redirects, ranges, browser caches, and origin credentials
requiredControls: exact origin allowlist and credentials policy
capability-bound cache identity, safe cache directives, validated redirects and response metadata
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Reject origin, principal, generation, range, or identity mismatch before bytes become application-visible.

boundaries.crossing: principal, deployment, application, source, typed scope, collections, columns, cache identity, and command capabilities
requiredControls: canonical typed scope encoding and domain-separated collision-resistant hashing through maintained libraries
exact equality checks with no prefix, delimiter-string, or client cache-key trust
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Return no dataset capability, stream, range, or command authority for an ambiguous or mismatched identity.

boundaries.crossing: signed grants, key identifiers, command capabilities, and monotonic authorization-generation updates
requiredControls: maintained signature library with algorithm allowlist and exact claim validation
durable monotonic generation and current-state check at every protected operation
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Unknown key, algorithm, version, clock state, issuer, audience, or generation blocks work.

boundaries.crossing: COPY snapshots, logical replication, relation metadata, epochs, and WAL feedback
requiredControls: least-privilege PostgreSQL identity and authenticated connection
exact-cut protocol, bounded normalization, replica-identity checks, current-owner fencing, and durable append before feedback
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Stop at the last complete cursor and require rebuild or operator action on unknown semantics, discontinuity, or stale ownership.

boundaries.crossing: immutable upload, catalog publication, exact-scope download capability, range request, and garbage collection
requiredControls: private bucket and least-privilege provider identity
short-lived exact-scope capability plus catalog-authenticated byte, length, schema, cursor, format, and digest verification
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Unpublished, mismatched, expired, revoked, corrupt, or orphaned objects remain inaccessible and inactive.

boundaries.crossing: normalized command kind, payload, principal, generation, mutation ID, idempotency record, business effects, and echo marker
requiredControls: explicit write capability and current authorization check
application validation plus one PostgreSQL transaction binding idempotency, effects, outcome, and canonical echo marker
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Reject or preserve transport ambiguity; never report canonical confirmation before the matching CDC echo.

boundaries.crossing: application-maintained denormalized authorized membership and projected business rows
requiredControls: application transactionally maintains projection consistency
Calque consumes the complete projection as canonical CDC without generic lookup joins
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Missing, ambiguous, cross-source, or stale projection semantics block publication or require rebuild.

boundaries.crossing: source, lockfiles, fork revisions, dependencies, toolchains, images, SBOM, and release evidence
requiredControls: immutable pinned inputs, provenance, vulnerability and license scanning, parser fuzzing, and reproducible candidate binding
independent security acceptance of the exact candidate with critical and high findings remediated and retested
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Mutable, unproven, vulnerable, mismatched, or unreviewed candidate cannot reach a release.

boundaries.crossing: logs, metrics, traces, backups, restores, keys, manifests, catalog, objects, source identity, and operational commands
requiredControls: least privilege, redaction, access control, bounded retention, authenticated backup, and one recovery-unit procedure
restore consistency checks, epoch replacement, readiness fencing, and tested upgrade and rollback
boundaries.failClosedBehavior: Inconsistent restore or unknown continuity keeps readiness false and forces a new epoch and rebuild.

revocationFences.start: The application authority durably advances the online monotonic authorization generation.
revocationFences.guarantee: No new forbidden bootstrap, artifact capability, range, stream open or resume, or command work is authorized under the old generation.
revocationFences.hostileObservationLimit: Bytes fully or partly disclosed before this durable fence cannot be retracted from a hostile browser.

revocationFences.start: A connected honest client receives the authenticated ordered revocation barrier.
revocationFences.guarantee: It locks every affected query before applying another affected transaction member, resolves pending mutations, clears resident state, and rebuilds from a safe grant.
revocationFences.hostileObservationLimit: A hostile browser may ignore deletion or query locks; the server disclosure fence remains the security authority.

revocationFences.start: The client loses the authenticated channel before receiving a newer generation barrier.
revocationFences.guarantee: An honest disconnected client stops stale local usability no later than the short-lived grant or lease expiry and must reauthorize before reconnect or resume.
revocationFences.hostileObservationLimit: Expiry cannot erase, disable, or make unreadable bytes already copied by a hostile browser.

residualDataPolicy.promise: Calque prevents new authorization after the server fence and removes or makes inaccessible affected state in an honest current client; it does not promise remote erasure of bytes already observed or copied.
coveredEvents: principal or tenant switch in a shared browser profile
backup, log, metric, trace, crash dump, and error retention
requiredBehavior: lock affected honest-client queries before clear and rebuild
partition and invalidate caches by exact authorized identity and generation
cancel or reauthorize in-flight work and pending commands
redact bearer material, secrets, row values, signed capabilities, and sensitive scope values from observability and errors
document retention and deletion behavior for privileged operational stores
unavoidableResiduals: copies made by a hostile browser before the disclosure fence
browser-managed freed memory, swap, crash reports, extensions, screenshots, exports, and developer tools outside Calque control
operator-controlled backups and logs retained according to the documented self-host policy
intermediary retention outside the declared authenticated private topology

prohibitedLocations: browser bundle, browser storage, artifact bytes, URLs, logs, metrics, traces, and container image layers
secretClasses.rotationBoundary: Key ID is explicit; verifiers accept only configured current or grace keys and unknown or retired keys fail closed.
secretClasses.failureBehavior: Compromise requires key removal, authorization-generation advancement, grant expiry, incident response, and affected-scope rebuild.

prohibitedLocations: browser, application JavaScript, artifact catalog, object metadata, logs, images, and generated source
secretClasses.rotationBoundary: Least-privilege replication and control credentials rotate through the documented readiness-fenced operation.
secretClasses.failureBehavior: Unknown or failed credential makes source readiness false; never fall back to a broader identity.

holders: artifact builder and delivery service runtime secret mounts
prohibitedLocations: browser, object URLs, catalog payload, logs, metrics, images, and generated source
secretClasses.rotationBoundary: Provider credentials are least privilege and rotate without making the bucket public.
secretClasses.failureBehavior: Storage readiness becomes false; no public-read fallback or unsigned object delivery is permitted.

holders: Calque server and migration runtime secret mounts
prohibitedLocations: browser, artifacts, URLs, logs, images, and application client code
secretClasses.rotationBoundary: Distinct runtime and migration privileges rotate with explicit migration and readiness checks.
secretClasses.failureBehavior: Control state becomes unavailable and protected operations fail closed.

prohibitedLocations: browser, source tree, container image layer, log, metric, trace, backup without encryption, and object artifact
secretClasses.rotationBoundary: Certificate and key replacement preserves validated hostname and trust-chain configuration.
secretClasses.failureBehavior: TLS endpoint is unavailable rather than downgraded to plaintext.

holders: authorized browser for its short lifetime
prohibitedLocations: logs, metrics, traces, referrer headers, shared cache keys, error messages, analytics, and long-lived browser persistence
secretClasses.rotationBoundary: Capabilities expire quickly, bind exact identity, scope, generation, origin, and object, and are reissued only after online authorization.
secretClasses.failureBehavior: Expiry, mismatch, replay outside binding, or revocation causes denial before new disclosure.

holders: operator-controlled protected backup and recovery system
prohibitedLocations: browser, public object storage, unauthenticated logs, images, and ordinary release evidence
secretClasses.rotationBoundary: Backup key custody and restore access are documented, independently access-controlled, and tested.
secretClasses.failureBehavior: Unavailable or inconsistent key material blocks restore; partial recovery does not become ready.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: The operator controls DNS, TLS termination, origins, firewalling, and private Docker networking and follows the documented supported topology.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: Traffic confidentiality, endpoint authenticity, and internal-service isolation may fail outside the product boundary.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Deployment preflight records origin topology, certificate validation, exposed ports, and network policy.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: PostgreSQL 18, the control store, and private S3-compatible storage are access-controlled, patched, and not exposed with default credentials.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: An infrastructure attacker may bypass Calque authorization or corrupt canonical and artifact state.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Readiness and security checks record versions, identities, bucket privacy, and privilege probes.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: The application backend correctly authenticates principals, evaluates business authorization, maintains projections, and validates business commands.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: Calque will faithfully synchronize or execute an application-authorized but semantically wrong scope or command.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Application integration tests and independent security review cover grant issuance, projection maintenance, and command policy.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: Host root, container runtime administrator, browser owner, and database superuser are outside the confidentiality boundary for data they administer.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: These actors can inspect memory, credentials, disks, traffic endpoints, or canonical rows and cannot be contained by Calque.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Documentation states the administrative trust boundary and prescribes separate least-privilege identities.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: System clocks used for grants, TLS, evidence, and expiry are monitored and stay synchronized; grant verification allows no clock skew.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: Grant validity, revocation expiry, TLS, or measurement claims may be wrong and protected work must stop.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Environment preflight records achieved clock synchronization and blocks outside tolerance.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: Signing keys, database credentials, object credentials, and backup keys are injected through protected runtime secret facilities and rotated after compromise.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: Attackers may forge grants or directly access privileged stores.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Secret scans, image inspection, runtime mount checks, rotation drills, and redaction tests pass.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: Backups include control state, canonical log, catalog, objects, signing material, manifests, and source identity as one consistency-checked recovery unit.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: A mismatched restore may be incomplete or authorize stale data and must force a new epoch rather than readiness.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Backup and restore fault tests prove consistent recovery or explicit epoch replacement.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: The immutable release candidate uses its pinned lockfiles, fork revision, images, and reviewed configuration without mutable tag substitution.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: Release evidence and independent review no longer bind the running software.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Deployment verifies source, dependency, image, profile, and evidence-index digests.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: Capacity and rate limits are sized for the declared workload; automatic HA and horizontal scaling are not assumed.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: Authorized or hostile demand may cause explicit unavailability, backlog rebuild, or capacity rejection.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Operations load tests record queue, disk, WAL, memory, and recovery bounds.

selfHostAssumptions.statement: Cloud accelerators are optional and the supported core runs on the documented cloud-neutral Docker composition.
selfHostAssumptions.failureEffect: Provider-specific behavior outside the provider conformance contract is unsupported.
selfHostAssumptions.operatorProof: Clean-host reproduction uses only the public Docker, PostgreSQL, and S3-compatible path.

abuseCases.action: Alter issuer, audience, deployment, application, source, principal, typed scope, collections, columns, schema, generation, time, key ID, or command claims in a grant.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Maintained signature verification and exact claim validation reject the grant before protected work.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any bootstrap, byte, stream, or command authorization is a critical authorization failure.
abuseCases.verification: Negative vector independently mutates every bound field and signature byte.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Compromise of the application signing key is handled operationally, not by signature verification.

abuseCases.action: Use prefix, case, Unicode, numeric/string, delimiter, null, ordering, or hash-collision ambiguity to obtain another scope.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Canonical typed encoding, domain separation, maintained collision-resistant hashing, and exact scope equality fail closed.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Cross-scope delivery is a critical tenant isolation failure.
abuseCases.verification: Golden and negative vectors cover type confusion, normalization, delimiters, reordered fields, and adversarial identifiers.
abuseCases.residualRisk: None while every scope is source-wide: a scope carries no application-defined values.

abuseCases.action: Reuse an expired, not-yet-valid, retired-key, wrong-version, or old-generation grant.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Clock, algorithm, key, version, expiry, and online generation checks run at every protected operation.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any new forbidden work after the server fence is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Freeze clock boundaries and attempt bootstrap, range, resume, stream, and command at both sides of each boundary.
abuseCases.residualRisk: A disconnected hostile browser retains previously received bytes.

abuseCases.action: Modify generated bindings, dependency graphs, queries, worker messages, cursors, collection IDs, status flags, or adapter state to widen coverage or fabricate completeness.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Server authorization ignores client coverage claims; client activation verifies authenticated catalog identity and complete cohort state.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Unauthorized delivery or application-visible false completeness violates the core security and correctness contract.
abuseCases.verification: Tamper every public and worker boundary while comparing visible state to the independent PostgreSQL oracle.
abuseCases.residualRisk: A hostile browser can render invented UI to its owner but cannot make the server disclose more data.

abuseCases.action: Replay a partial, corrupt, oversized, wrong-format, wrong-cursor, wrong-schema, or wrong-scope artifact into the materializer.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Authenticated catalog metadata, encoded and decoded bounds, structural validation, and digest checks occur before activation.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Parsing before bounds or any partial publication is a critical integrity or capacity failure.
abuseCases.verification: Mutate every identity field and byte region, truncate every stage, and exercise decompression expansion and malformed structures.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Parser implementation vulnerabilities remain subject to fuzzing and independent review.

abuseCases.action: Forge or reorder cursors, transaction fragments, revocation barriers, mutation echoes, duplicates, gaps, or relation versions.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Opaque epoch-bound cursors, authenticated ordered messages, complete transaction framing, idempotency, and explicit rebuild boundaries reject ambiguity.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Mixed state, confirmation without canonical echo, or skip-and-continue is forbidden.
abuseCases.verification: Fragment, duplicate, reorder, omit, replay, and cross-epoch inject every message class.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Authenticated endpoint compromise is outside the message-authentication boundary.

abuseCases.action: Downgrade TLS, redirect to an attacker host, present an invalid certificate, or force plaintext fallback.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Validated TLS, hostname and trust-chain checks, safe redirect policy, and no plaintext fallback.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Connection fails before credentials or data are transmitted.
abuseCases.verification: Exercise wrong host, untrusted CA, expired certificate, redirect chain, mixed content, and unavailable TLS.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Operator-installed malicious trust roots are administrative compromise.

abuseCases.action: Use permissive CORS, CSRF, origin reflection, DNS rebinding, Host confusion, or credentialed cross-site requests.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Exact configured origins, credential policy, CSRF defenses for state changes, validated Host and forwarded headers, and rebinding-resistant deployment configuration.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Cross-origin read or command authorization is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Attack from null, sibling, suffix, mixed-scheme, redirected, rebinding, and unlisted origins with and without credentials.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Malicious script already executing in an allowed application origin has that origin's browser authority.

abuseCases.action: Delay, duplicate, fragment, truncate, reorder, stall, or replay HTTP and live-stream traffic.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Bounded timeouts and frames, resumable verified transport, transaction ordering, idempotency, and explicit rebuild on gaps.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Availability may degrade, but no false complete state or reordered canonical truth may appear.
abuseCases.verification: Network fault matrix covers each fault at bootstrap, range, catch-up, active stream, revocation, and command response.
abuseCases.residualRisk: A network attacker can deny service within upstream capacity.

abuseCases.action: Substitute another tenant's principal, source, scope, artifact, cache entry, stream resume token, or mutation ID.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Every identity is bound to deployment, application, source, principal, typed scope, generation, schema, and capability purpose.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Cross-tenant disclosure or command effect is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Cartesian negative matrix swaps one identity dimension at a time and across concurrent tenants.
abuseCases.residualRisk: An application backend that intentionally co-authorizes tenants owns that policy.

abuseCases.action: Cause overlapping shared partitions or duplicate primary keys to smuggle rows into a union scope.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Not served in the pre-alpha: every scope is source-wide, so no shared partitions exist to overlap and no union scope is formed.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Unregistered union or ambiguous membership blocks activation.
abuseCases.verification: None while every scope is source-wide.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Application-owned projection bugs remain an application authorization risk.

abuseCases.action: Race revocation against bootstrap, artifact issue, open range, stream resume, catch-up, command validation, execution, or retry.
abuseCases.expectedControl: The durable generation advancement is the disclosure fence and every new protected operation checks current generation.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any newly authorized forbidden work after the fence is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Barrier-controlled schedules place the fence before and after each authorization and I/O boundary.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Bytes already authorized and disclosed before the fence cannot be retracted.

abuseCases.action: Receive revocation amid a multi-collection transaction, query notification, optimistic mutation, clear, or rebuild.
abuseCases.expectedControl: The authenticated ordered barrier locks all affected queries before another member applies, then safely resolves mutations, clears, and rebuilds.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any post-receipt affected query result or mixed-cursor callback is forbidden.
abuseCases.verification: Exhaustive small-state and randomized schedules inspect every application-observable callback.
abuseCases.residualRisk: A hostile browser may refuse to lock or clear its own memory.

abuseCases.action: Remain disconnected beyond authorization narrowing or reconnect using a stale grant and resume cursor.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Short grant or lease expiry bounds honest stale usability; reconnect and resume reauthorize online.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Stale query usability beyond expiry or new delivery without reauthorization is forbidden.
abuseCases.verification: Control clocks and connectivity across expiry, suspension, wake, reload, and reconnect boundaries.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Previously copied bytes remain readable to a hostile browser.

abuseCases.action: Log out or switch principal in a shared browser and recover prior tenant data from memory, workers, HTTP cache, IndexedDB-like application storage, errors, or open responses.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Current honest client locks, cancels, clears all Calque-owned resident state, partitions cache identity, and refuses stale response activation.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: New-principal application visibility of prior data is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Shared-profile tests switch principals during every hydration and live state and inspect all Calque-owned storage and callbacks.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Browser internals, extensions, screenshots, exports, and hostile copies are not erasable promises.

abuseCases.action: Expose grants, capabilities, rows, scope values, credentials, signing material, or command payloads through logs, metrics, traces, errors, crash dumps, support bundles, or backups.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Field-level redaction, allowlisted telemetry, access-controlled retention, secret scanning, and explicit backup custody prevent ordinary observability disclosure.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Sensitive material in a prohibited sink blocks security release.
abuseCases.verification: Canary secrets and rows traverse every success and error path; scanners assert absence from each sink and image layer.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Privileged operators with authorized backup access remain inside the administrative trust boundary.

abuseCases.action: Send oversized, deeply nested, fragmented, compressed-expansion, high-cardinality, slow, repeated, or malformed protocol inputs.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Limits apply before allocation and decompression; maintained bounded parsers, deadlines, quotas, concurrency controls, and rate limits reject work.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: The request may fail, but process-wide unbounded memory, CPU, disk, queue, or partial publication is forbidden.
abuseCases.verification: Tests exercise real allocation and parser pressure at every encoded and decoded boundary.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Distributed demand can cause bounded unavailability on a single-server deployment.

abuseCases.action: Create a scope or query dependency set whose complete authorized collection cannot fit the client or preparation budget.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Server and client capacity accounting reject before unsafe allocation and return no partial dataset.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Structured capacity rejection is acceptable; crash, partial visibility, or resource starvation of unrelated tenants is not.
abuseCases.verification: Real below-limit and over-limit profiles measure browser, server, storage, and queue allocations.
abuseCases.residualRisk: A physically valid but large authorized scope may be unavailable on the declared client.

abuseCases.action: Stampede artifact preparation, range requests, scope variants, reconnects, and cache misses or hold slow downloads open.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Deduplicated fenced builds, exact capabilities, bounded concurrency, rate limits, timeouts, LRU/retirement rules, and per-identity accounting.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Bounded rejection or delay is acceptable; cross-tenant eviction, unbounded durable objects, or stale publication is not.
abuseCases.verification: A runtime scope load test applies concurrent cold, revoked, abandoned, duplicate, and adversarial scope demand.
abuseCases.residualRisk: The single active server has a documented finite availability envelope.

abuseCases.action: Produce sustained or burst CDC above client, server, canonical-log, storage, or WAL retention capacity.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Bounded queues, ordered backpressure, drain limits, monitoring, and deterministic snapshot rebuild boundaries prevent unbounded growth.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Explicit degraded availability or rebuild is acceptable; loss, reordering, silent skip, or indefinite growth is not.
abuseCases.verification: Sustained and burst schedules measure queue, disk, WAL, lag, recovery, and reference convergence.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Source write rate beyond the declared envelope can require operator action.

abuseCases.action: Search bundles, source maps, generated definitions, worker messages, URLs, errors, storage, and artifacts for server credentials or signing keys.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Only short-lived scoped delivery material reaches the browser; secret scans and negative runtime inspection cover all public outputs.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any long-lived server, database, storage, TLS, backup, or signing secret in the browser is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Build and runtime secret canaries are scanned across public files, requests, responses, memory messages, and storage.
abuseCases.residualRisk: An authorized browser necessarily holds current data and a short-lived grant or delivery capability.

abuseCases.action: Exfiltrate build, registry, signing, or deployment secrets through install scripts, build plugins, source maps, images, or test logs.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Pinned reviewed dependencies, least-privilege isolated build credentials, secret scanning, image inspection, provenance, and independent review.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Secret exposure or unreviewed network-active build input blocks release.
abuseCases.verification: Inspect dependency scripts, build network policy, image history, artifacts, evidence logs, and canary leakage.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Compromise of the build executor administrator is a privileged infrastructure incident.

abuseCases.action: Guess, replay, share, or substitute an object URL or capability across principal, tenant, origin, generation, object, range, or expiry.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Private storage plus server-authorized short-lived exact-scope capability binding rejects every mismatch; URL entropy alone grants nothing.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Cross-binding byte delivery is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Swap every binding independently, exercise leakage through referrer and logs, and retry before and after revocation and expiry.
abuseCases.residualRisk: A hostile authorized browser can copy bytes received while its capability is valid.

abuseCases.action: Poison or confuse shared caches using omitted Vary dimensions, ranges, redirects, validation metadata, stale responses, or partial-content combinations.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Authenticated artifact identity and digests are independent of cache metadata: the plan binds the whole-artifact SHA-256 and the SHA-256 of each 4 MiB chunk, which the server computes from the bytes it verified against the whole digest, and the client verifies every byte against the chunk digests before it parses any; exact cache identity and safe range semantics prevent cross-scope activation.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: A poisoned response fails before parsing or activation and cannot become a plausible complete collection.
abuseCases.verification: Cache matrix varies principal, origin, generation, scope, schema, encoding, range, ETag-like metadata, and response age.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Cache denial of service remains possible without integrity loss.

abuseCases.action: Make the bucket public, grant list access, use overbroad provider credentials, or trust provider metadata as artifact authenticity.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Provider conformance and deployment preflight require private access and least privilege; Calque authenticates content against trusted catalog metadata.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Public or overbroad object access fails readiness and security gates.
abuseCases.verification: Anonymous, cross-identity, list, overwrite, metadata mutation, and provider credential probes run against the deployed composition.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Object-store or host administrator can access stored bytes by definition.

abuseCases.action: Invoke a write with only a read grant or change command kind, payload, source, principal, generation, or mutation identity.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Explicit command capability, current server authorization, schema validation, and normalized payload binding reject escalation.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Unauthorized business effect is critical; optimistic client state must roll back.
abuseCases.verification: Negative command matrix mutates every authority and payload field and compares PostgreSQL effects.
abuseCases.residualRisk: An application backend that grants an unsafe command owns its business policy.

abuseCases.action: Retry a mutation after lost response, reuse its ID with a different payload, race duplicates, or replay it after principal or generation change.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Transactional idempotency record binds application, principal, generation, command kind, normalized payload hash, outcome, business effects, and echo marker.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: At most one business effect occurs; mismatched reuse is rejected and HTTP never falsely confirms canonical state.
abuseCases.verification: Concurrent and sequential retry schedules include crash before and after commit, lost response, echo delay, and mismatched reuse.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Mutation records require documented retention sufficient to cover the supported retry window.

abuseCases.action: Queue, send, commit, reject, echo, reload, or revoke several optimistic mutations in adversarial order.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Canonical CDC base plus ordered overlays, matching echo confirmation, deterministic rollback and replay, and revocation handling match the reference reducer.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Optimistic state may be temporary but cannot become false canonical truth or resurrect unauthorized effects.
abuseCases.verification: Exhaustive and randomized reducer equivalence covers every mutation lifecycle state and canonical interleaving.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Transient in-memory queued writes are lost on browser process loss by pre-alpha design.

abuseCases.action: Update a business row and its visibility projection non-atomically or emit incomplete projected data.
abuseCases.expectedControl: The application maintains sync-ready projection consistency in PostgreSQL; Calque applies only complete canonical transactions and the reference oracle checks membership and row data.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: A semantically wrong application projection is an application authorization defect; Calque must not invent a generic lookup fix.
abuseCases.verification: Projection fixtures cover gain, loss, key change, delete, truncate, transaction rollback, and concurrent business updates.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Correctness of application-specific business policy remains the application's responsibility.

abuseCases.action: Create adversarial identifiers, duplicate keys, null scope, key changes, truncates, TOAST values, or relation changes in a projection.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Frozen schema, replica identity, typed scope, normalization, complete transaction handling, and explicit incompatible-schema rebuild prevent ambiguity.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Unknown or ambiguous semantics stop at the last complete cursor; no row is skipped.
abuseCases.verification: PostgreSQL 18 fixtures exercise every value and DDL boundary through snapshot and CDC.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Unsupported PostgreSQL semantics produce availability loss by explicit design.

abuseCases.action: Configure a collection that performs cross-source, arbitrary live SQL, or generic CDC-time joins outside the pre-alpha model.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Static manifest compilation and generated dependency validation accept one-table or sync-ready projection collections from exactly one source.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Configuration fails before deployment or query activation.
abuseCases.verification: Negative manifests cover every cross-source and unsupported collection/query form.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Application code may independently combine data outside the Calque public query contract.

abuseCases.action: Substitute a mutable image tag, dependency, lockfile, fork revision, toolchain, generated file, or release evidence after review.
abuseCases.expectedControl: The immutable candidate binds source, dependencies, fork, images, profiles, artifacts, and evidence by digest; deployment and release closure verify equality.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any mismatch invalidates dependent evidence and blocks release.
abuseCases.verification: Mutation tests alter each bound input independently and require release-verifier rejection.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Compromise of every independent trust and signing root is outside the declared review model.

abuseCases.action: Exploit a vulnerable compression, protocol, crypto, database, URL, or parser dependency or a hand-written substitute.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Maintained libraries, pinned versions, SBOM, vulnerability scanning, malformed-input tests, fuzzing, upgrade cadence, and independent review are mandatory.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Unresolved critical or high vulnerability or unknown primitive blocks release.
abuseCases.verification: Scan the exact candidate and exercise parser corpora, fuzz targets, advisories, fork policy, and remediation retest.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Unknown zero-day vulnerabilities remain possible and require incident response.

abuseCases.action: Deploy a locally modified or stale candidate while presenting evidence from the reviewed release tree.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Runtime image and build digests must match the immutable evidence index and signed external acceptance.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Candidate mismatch is INVALID or BLOCKED evidence, never release PASS.
abuseCases.verification: Clean-host reproduction and release closure compare every candidate-binding digest.
abuseCases.residualRisk: An operator may knowingly run unsupported modified software but cannot inherit release claims.

abuseCases.action: Reach PostgreSQL, control database, object storage, metrics, debug, or administration ports directly.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Only intended public endpoints are exposed; private networking, firewall rules, authentication, and least-privilege identities protect internal services.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Unauthenticated internal reachability fails deployment security.
abuseCases.verification: Scan all host interfaces and Docker networks and attempt anonymous and default-credential access.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Host network administrator is privileged within the self-host trust boundary.

abuseCases.action: Use user-controlled URLs, paths, redirects, object names, callback targets, or source addresses to trigger SSRF, traversal, local-file access, or internal network access.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Typed configuration, strict URL and path parsing through maintained libraries, scheme and destination allowlists, canonical paths, and no browser-selected infrastructure endpoints.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any access outside the configured root or network policy is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Attack alternate schemes, encodings, IPv4 and IPv6 forms, redirects, DNS changes, traversal, separators, symlinks, and metadata endpoints.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Operator-configured trusted internal endpoints are within the deployment boundary.

abuseCases.action: Run containers as root, grant broad host mounts or capabilities, reuse credentials, or omit resource and filesystem restrictions.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Documented composition uses non-root least privilege, minimal capabilities, scoped mounts and identities, private ports, resource limits, and writable paths only where required.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Deployment preflight blocks unsupported insecure configuration.
abuseCases.verification: Inspect effective container users, capabilities, mounts, seccomp-like policy where supported, networks, credentials, and resource limits.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Container runtime and host kernel compromise are outside application isolation guarantees.

abuseCases.action: Restore control state, canonical log, catalog, objects, keys, manifests, or PostgreSQL source from inconsistent points in time.
abuseCases.expectedControl: One recovery-unit validation detects inconsistency, keeps readiness false, creates a new epoch, and forces safe rebuild.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Serving stale or mismatched state as current is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Restore fault matrix independently omits, rolls back, corrupts, and cross-combines every recovery component.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Loss of every consistent backup may cause accepted data unavailability and full resnapshot.

abuseCases.action: Allow a stale server owner to append, index, publish, garbage-collect, send WAL feedback, or issue client data after failover or restart.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Durable fencing and epoch identity permit only the current active owner at every side-effect boundary.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Stale-owner side effect is a critical canonical-truth failure.
abuseCases.verification: Pause and resume old owners around every durable and external side effect while a new owner starts.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Automatic high availability is outside the pre-alpha; recovery may require bounded downtime.

abuseCases.action: Exploit error recovery, cancellation, reload, worker crash, tab duplication, or backpressure to make a plausible partial state visible.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Private staging, one visibility epoch, complete-transaction cursor advancement, cancellation fences, and rebuild boundaries expose old-or-new complete state only.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Any application callback observing partial or mixed state is critical even if final convergence succeeds.
abuseCases.verification: Real-Chrome failpoints inspect every query, status, notification, derived query, and worker lifecycle boundary.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Multiple tabs may independently allocate and materialize; shared cross-tab state is not claimed.

abuseCases.action: Exploit algorithm confusion, missing key ID, duplicate claims, non-canonical encoding, permissive parsing, or unknown grant version.
abuseCases.expectedControl: A maintained library verifies an explicit algorithm allowlist and strict schema; duplicate, unknown required, ambiguous, or non-canonical claims fail closed.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: Acceptance of ambiguous or attacker-selected verification semantics is critical.
abuseCases.verification: Cross-implementation negative corpus includes algorithm, key, encoding, duplicate-field, truncation, and unknown-version cases.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Cryptographic implementation defects are reduced by maintained libraries and external review, not eliminated.

abuseCases.action: Supply prototype-polluting, deeply nested, oversized, type-confused, unknown-field, duplicate-key, numeric-boundary, or malformed command payloads.
abuseCases.expectedControl: Bounded strict schema decoding and application validation occur before authorization-dependent execution; unknown or ambiguous input is rejected.
abuseCases.failureOutcome: No business effect, secret leakage, process corruption, or unbounded resource use may occur.
abuseCases.verification: Malformed and boundary corpus plus fuzzing crosses public decoder, executor adapter, idempotency hash, and PostgreSQL binding.
abuseCases.residualRisk: Application command implementations require their own domain-specific validation and review.

nonClaims.statement: Calque does not erase or retract bytes already observed, copied, exported, screenshotted, cached, or retained by a hostile browser.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Use short grants, narrow scopes, server revocation, endpoint security, and data-governance controls; do not represent revocation as retroactive secrecy.

nonClaims.statement: The browser, its owner, extensions, DevTools, operating system, swap, crash reporting, and physical device are not trusted confidentiality boundaries for authorized client data.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Do not synchronize data that the authenticated user and administered device may not inspect.

nonClaims.statement: Calque does not correct wrong business authorization, projection membership, or unsafe business command semantics issued by the trusted application backend.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Audit and test application authorization, projections, and command handlers as part of the application security program.

nonClaims.statement: The pre-alpha does not provide automatic failover, Byzantine replication, horizontal scaling, multi-region continuity, or protection from host-root, database-superuser, object-store-admin, or container-runtime-admin compromise.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Protect and monitor the self-host infrastructure and accept bounded downtime or rebuild during recovery.

nonClaims.statement: The pre-alpha does not provide cross-source query atomicity or authorization, remote predicates, pagination, arbitrary server SQL, generic CDC-time joins, or durable offline mutation safety.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Keep each public query cohort on one source, maintain sync-ready projections, and treat transient queued writes as volatile.

nonClaims.statement: Object URL secrecy, bucket metadata, cache behavior, client-provided cache keys, TLS alone, and unguessable identifiers are not authorization or artifact-integrity systems.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Keep storage private and require exact online authorization plus trusted catalog verification for every delivery path.

nonClaims.statement: Denial-of-service immunity is not claimed; the pre-alpha has one active server per source and finite client, server, storage, queue, disk, and WAL budgets.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Apply finite limits and rate controls, monitor saturation, and accept explicit rejection, rebuild, or temporary unavailability beyond the envelope.

nonClaims.statement: Calque does not invent cryptographic, compression, URL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, protocol, or parser primitives and does not claim zero vulnerabilities.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Use maintained reviewed libraries, pin them, scan and fuzz the immutable candidate, and operate an upgrade and incident-response process.

nonClaims.statement: Compatibility beyond PostgreSQL 18, stable headed Chrome, the 16 GiB one-tab client, and the documented Docker/S3-compatible topology is not a pre-alpha security or correctness claim.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Treat other platforms, versions, stores, multiple active tabs, and provider-specific accelerators as unqualified until separately proven.

nonClaims.statement: A fast or visually plausible result, successful HTTP mutation response, final convergence, or self-reported client state does not prove completeness, authorization, canonical confirmation, or security.
nonClaims.operatorConsequence: Require the independent PostgreSQL oracle, authenticated canonical echo, adversarial fault results, and exact immutable-candidate evidence for claims.
